source.title: Learning sparse features can lead to overfitting in neural networks
source.authors: Leonardo Petrini; Francesco Cagnetta; E. Vanden-Eijnden; M. Wyart

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present, though some extracted equations and figure layouts are visibly garbled.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares feature learning with lazy training on generalization error and measures predictor sensitivity to image deformations, using its own methods and settings. It does not test any of the eight specifically mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports feature-versus-lazy test-error comparisons on image datasets and on synthetic sphere tasks, plus relative sensitivity to diffeomorphisms and other image transformations. These findings bear on generalization and properties associated with it, but none measures the behavior named in V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The study tests feature learning versus lazy training, not any of V1–V8. Its own experiments compare training regimes within fully connected networks and measure sensitivity to input transformations. Discussion of convolutional architectures does not provide an architectural comparison testing V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that sparse feature learning can harm generalization when task invariances or smooth variations are poorly captured by the architecture. Their sphere experiments support predicted learning-curve scaling, and their fully connected image experiments show worse test error and greater diffeomorphism sensitivity with feature learning. The proposed causal explanation for image performance remains plausible rather than established.
record.recipe_differences: Compares mean-field feature learning and lazy NTK training in shallow fully connected ReLU networks, plus image-classification sensitivity measurements; it does not reproduce any of the mapped versions' interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The generalization comparison depends on training regime, target smoothness, input dimension, dataset, and training-set size. Relative sensitivity also varies with transformation type and training regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Lazy training gives lower test error than feature learning for the fully connected classifiers on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lazy training can generalize better than feature learning in fully connected image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: For constant sphere targets, predicted feature/lazy error-decay exponents are 4/4 at d=2, 2.5/3 at d=3, and 1.75/2.5 at d=5; numerical curves support these predictions subject to finite-time effects.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relative learning-curve scaling of feature and lazy training depends on input dimension and target smoothness.

fits_no_version.finding: Lazy predictors have lower relative sensitivity to small diffeomorphisms on all three image datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lazy training yields smoother fully connected image predictors along the studied diffeomorphisms.

fits_no_version.finding: On Fashion-MNIST, lazy predictors are less sensitive to translations, while feature predictors are less sensitive to boundary corruption relative to whole-image noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relative transformation sensitivity of feature and lazy predictors depends on the transformation.

record.problems: Image results use shallow fully connected networks and do not compare against convolutional networks. Figure-only plots provide no exact values or error bars for the image test-error and sensitivity curves. The paper notes finite-training-time effects for feature learning in d=2 and that exact minimal-norm solutions may be computationally infeasible to reach.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for additional conditions beyond the reported image datasets and sphere dimensions; the paper includes further target-smoothness curves in Figure G.1, but these do not map to the listed claim versions and are omitted from the capped extraction.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error; training-set-size sweeps do not test this.
Convolutional-versus-fully-connected test performance, local-connectivity contributions, and sparse or transferred initialization conditions.
Adaptive-versus-SGD optimizer generalization and effects of tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- or margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is warranted for V1–V8. Infinite-width training and sparsity do not establish V2 or V3. Excerpt E2 concerns R7–R9, not its assigned R1–R3.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label evaluation.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison; the image experiments use fully connected networks.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.
